name: stage_handtuned_proto_steps_v1_gaitcycle_v3
description: v3 of the gait-cycle A/B — adaptive thresholds (matches feedback_no_tuning: 'add the adaptive mechanism that would set [the bar] from the system's own dynamics'). The reward bar floats as a fraction of EMAs of the body's own observed cycle statistics: eff_min_progress = max(static_floor=1mm, 0.5 * progress_ema); eff_max_backward = max(static_floor=3mm, 2.0 * wobble_ema). After 20-cycle warmup (~30 sec at v1's observed cycle rate of ~40/min), the bar locks to the body's actual capability and pressures 'better-than-typical' cycles. Floor values kept tiny so adaptive takes over fast. Hypothesis: this resolves both the v1 failure (bar too tight for actual motion) and v2's open question (whether ANY static value can match a body whose cycle statistics drift as the policy learns) — the bar follows the body. Trajectory diag adds: progress_ema, wobble_ema, eff_min_progress, eff_max_backward, attempts_total.
